title: Honest Inference for Hard-Clamp Policies on a Continuous Treatment Vector
banked_reason: D0.5 kernel_substituted@oeq:exact-rough-order: exact rough-phase minimax orders, observable attaining procedure, and matching converse remain absent; math panel passed the partial results, but the achieved incremental tier is below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The proposal's promised exact rough-phase minimax risk and honest-length orders are replaced by a polynomial-exponent result and a nonmatching subpolynomial sandwich; the named observable attaining procedure and matching lower bound for the exact factor remain absent.
No observable procedure is shown to attain the lower-envelope scale, and no converse rules out improvement over the nearest-neighbor upper bound.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established identification, an observable upper bound, the exact ordinary phase, and a same-class quantitative rough-phase lower envelope of n^(-tau) exp(-C sqrt(log n)). The D0.5 math panel passed these partial results, but its rubric found that the promised exact rough-phase order had been left as an open question. A future retry needs an explicit multiresolution estimator and matching converse under the unchanged arbitrary-density class; repeating the open obligation is not a repair.
tldr: A hard clamp of the first coordinate of a continuous treatment vector moves positive probability onto a face whose tangential weight is an unknown functional of an otherwise arbitrary dependent treatment density. Full-process conditional randomization and structural-mean continuity identify the causal value as an ordinary retained-outcome term plus this weighted face trace. The project proves a fully observable density-free estimator and honest interval, the exact ordinary phase including the elbow at \(\beta_2=1/2\), and same-class joint density-regression mixture converses. In the rough phase it proves the common polynomial exponent and the bounds \(c n^{-\tau}\exp\{-C\sqrt{\log n}\} \leq R_n\wedge H_n \leq R_n\vee H_n \leq C n^{-\tau}\). The exact constant-factor orders and whether the two criteria share a nonconstant subpolynomial factor remain open.
gap: Chen and Gao analyze submanifold regression integrals with a known weight and obtain a feasible rate match only above their sieve smoothness threshold. Jiang et al. require blockwise smooth invertibility of the vector policy. The banked one-dose clamp theorem has no rough tangent, while discrete polynomial estimators do not face a shrinking normal strip.
fill: The project keeps the exact nonsmooth policy and the same arbitrary-density class, constructs an observable estimator and bias-aware interval, and pairs them with same-class all-procedure lower mixtures. The open centerpiece is a matching multiresolution approximation-and-variance theorem that determines the exact factor for both decision criteria.
